specPoints.text: know that a hydrocarbon is a compound of hydrogen and carbon only
understand how to represent organic molecules using empirical formulae, molecular formulae, general formulae, structural formulae and displayed formulae
know what is meant by the terms homologous series, functional group and isomerism
understand how to write the possible structural and displayed formulae of an organic molecule given its molecular formula

primer.text: From covalent bonding you already know that non-metal atoms share pairs of electrons, and carbon is famous for chaining with itself. This note opens organic chemistry: what counts as an organic compound, the hydrocarbon rule, five ways of drawing the same molecule, and the family language chemists use for it all.

lessons.title: Organic chemistry and the hydrocarbon rule
lessons.opening: Organic chemistry studies the compounds built around carbon, from fuels to plastics. Its simplest members contain just two elements, and that two-element rule is what this lesson pins down first.
keyPoints: Organic chemistry studies carbon-containing compounds, their structures, their properties and their reactions.
Metal carbonates, carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide are excluded from organic chemistry by convention.
A hydrocarbon is a compound whose molecules contain hydrogen and carbon atoms and no other element.
The word only matters in the definition, so a molecule with oxygen present is not a hydrocarbon.
Hydrocarbons matter because fuels such as petrol and natural gas are built from them.

low.restatement: Organic chemistry is the study of carbon compounds. A hydrocarbon is the simplest kind: its molecules hold hydrogen and carbon atoms and nothing else.
low.analogy: Think of carbon as the frame of a bicycle and hydrogen as everything bolted on; a hydrocarbon is a bike built from exactly those two parts and no extras.
low.examPointer: When defining a hydrocarbon, state that hydrogen and carbon are the only elements present, or the marking point is lost.

medium.restatement: Organic chemistry is the study of the structure, properties and reactions of carbon compounds, with metal carbonates, carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide left out by convention. A hydrocarbon is a compound of hydrogen and carbon with no third element allowed.
medium.analogy: A hydrocarbon molecule is like a lego model built from exactly two brick colours; the moment a third colour appears, the model has left the hydrocarbon family for good.
medium.examPointer: Quote the only-elements rule when defining a hydrocarbon, and expect a follow-up asking why carbon dioxide does not qualify.

options.text: A compound containing carbon and hydrogen only
options.explanation: Both elements present and no third element is exactly what the hydrocarbon rule requires.

options.text: Carbon dioxide, because it contains carbon
options.explanation: Carbon dioxide contains oxygen as well, so it breaks the only-two-elements rule and is excluded by convention too.

options.text: A compound of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen
options.explanation: The extra oxygen disqualifies it; a hydrocarbon may not carry any third element.

options.text: Calcium carbonate, because carbon is in the name
options.explanation: Metal carbonates are conventionally excluded from organic chemistry, and oxygen is present as well.

check.stem: Why are carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide left out of organic chemistry?

options.text: They are excluded by convention, like metal carbonates
options.explanation: The syllabus convention simply lists these small oxides as outside organic chemistry despite their carbon.

options.text: They contain no carbon atoms at all
options.explanation: Both are oxides of carbon; the exclusion is by convention, not by their formula.

options.text: They are too reactive to study in a laboratory
options.explanation: Reactivity is irrelevant; the split is a naming convention of the subject.

options.text: They only exist as gases at room temperature
options.explanation: Physical state does not decide the boundary; the convention does.

check.stem: A molecule contains 4 carbon atoms, 10 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom. How is it classified?

options.text: An organic compound, but not a hydrocarbon
options.explanation: It is carbon-based so organic, but the oxygen atom breaks the hydrocarbon rule.

options.text: A hydrocarbon, because it is mostly hydrogen and carbon
options.explanation: Mostly is not enough; the single oxygen atom still breaks the only-two-elements rule.

options.text: Not organic, because oxygen is present
options.explanation: Oxygen-containing carbon compounds can be organic; only the hydrocarbon label is lost.

options.text: A metal carbonate, because oxygen is bonded to carbon
options.explanation: There is no metal present, so the carbonate category does not apply.

check.stem: Which statement about organic chemistry is correct?

options.text: It is the study of the structure, properties and reactions of carbon compounds
options.explanation: That trio of interests is exactly how the subject is defined in the note.

options.text: It studies every compound that contains hydrogen
options.explanation: Hydrogen alone never qualifies a compound; carbon is the organising element.

options.text: It only studies compounds extracted from living things
options.explanation: The historical origin of the name does not restrict the modern subject.

options.text: It excludes compounds that burn in air
options.explanation: Burning behaviour is irrelevant; combustion is itself an organic reaction type studied in the topic.

check.stem: Methane burns in oxygen to give carbon dioxide and water. Is methane a hydrocarbon?

options.text: Yes, because methane itself contains hydrogen and carbon only
options.explanation: The molecule CH4 carries just those two elements, whatever reactions it later undergoes.

options.text: No, because burning it produces oxygen-containing products
options.explanation: The classification depends on the molecule itself, not on the products of one reaction.

options.text: No, because oxygen took part in the reaction
options.explanation: Reacting with oxygen does not change what methane is made of before the reaction.

options.text: Yes, because carbon dioxide is also organic
options.explanation: Carbon dioxide is not organic; the yes answer rests on methane alone.

lessons.title: Five ways to represent the same molecule
lessons.opening: One molecule can be written five different ways, and each way trades detail for convenience. This lesson walks through empirical, molecular, general, displayed and structural representations so you can pick the right one on demand.
keyPoints: An empirical formula shows the simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms in a molecule.
A molecular formula counts the actual number of each type of atom in one molecule.
A general formula describes a whole family of compounds using the letter n, such as CnH2n+2 for alkanes.
A displayed formula shows every atom and every bond, including their spatial arrangement.
A structural formula leaves most bonds out, keeping only the key ones plus bracketed side groups.

low.restatement: The five representations are a ladder of detail. Empirical gives ratios, molecular gives counts, general covers a family, displayed draws every bond, and structural sketches the important parts only. Pick the one the question asks for, and check which bonds it must show.
low.analogy: It is like describing a house five ways: a pie-chart of materials, an inventory of rooms, a blueprint template for estates, a full photo, and a quick sketch of the walls that matter.
low.examPointer: Match the representation to the command word: count atoms for molecular, draw every bond for displayed.

medium.restatement: Empirical formulae compress a molecule to its simplest atom ratio, while molecular formulae state the true atom counts. General formulae use n to describe a homologous family; displayed formulae draw all bonds and atoms in their spatial arrangement, and structural formulae omit most bonds, showing key multiple bonds and bracketed groups.
medium.analogy: A crowd photo, a head-count, a family portrait template, a zoomed portrait showing every face, and a group photo with only the leaders in focus tell the same people story at five zoom levels, just like the five formulae tell one molecule story.
medium.examPointer: When asked for a displayed formula, draw every bond explicitly; brackets and missing C-H bonds belong to structural formulae and lose the mark.

check.stem: Hydrogen peroxide has the molecular formula H2O2. What is its empirical formula?

options.text: HO
options.explanation: Dividing both subscripts by two gives the simplest ratio, one hydrogen to one oxygen.

options.text: H2O2, because the molecular formula is already simplest
options.explanation: The subscripts share a factor of two, so the ratio is not yet in its simplest form.

options.text: H2O
options.explanation: That is water, a different substance; ratios are reduced, not rewritten as a known compound.

options.text: HO2
options.explanation: The ratio must keep one oxygen per one hydrogen after cancelling, not redistribute the atoms.

check.stem: Which representation shows every bond and atom in their spatial arrangement?

options.text: The displayed formula
options.explanation: Displayed formulae draw all atoms and all bonds, which is why they are also called graphical formulae.

options.text: The empirical formula
options.explanation: An empirical formula is just a ratio of element counts, with no bonds drawn at all.

options.text: The structural formula
options.explanation: Structural formulae deliberately omit most bonds and only highlight key ones.

options.text: The general formula
options.explanation: A general formula describes a whole family with the letter n, not one drawn molecule.

check.stem: A molecule has the molecular formula C4H10. Which statement follows?

options.text: Its displayed formula would show 4 carbon and 10 hydrogen atoms with all bonds drawn
options.explanation: Displayed formulae reproduce the molecular count and draw every bond joining the atoms.

options.text: Its empirical formula must also be C4H10
options.explanation: The ratio 4:10 simplifies to 2:5, so the empirical formula is C2H5.

options.text: It must be a straight chain with no branches
options.explanation: The molecular formula fixes atom counts but says nothing about branching arrangements.

options.text: It cannot be drawn as a displayed formula because it is too large
options.explanation: Size is no barrier; displayed formulae exist precisely to draw the full bonding picture.

check.stem: What does the n do in the general formula CnH2n+2?

options.text: It stands for a varying whole number, one value per family member
options.explanation: Substituting successive whole numbers generates each member of the alkane family in turn.

options.text: It is the charge on the molecule
options.explanation: The letter n counts carbon atoms; it has nothing to do with charge.

options.text: It is fixed at 6 for every organic compound
options.explanation: The whole point of n is that it varies as you move along the family.

options.text: It counts only the hydrogen atoms
options.explanation: The subscript on carbon is n, so n counts carbon atoms and the hydrogen count follows.

check.stem: Why does a structural formula place CH3 groups in brackets?

options.text: To gather identical repeated groups so the chain stays clear without drawing every bond
options.explanation: Brackets with a subscript compress repeats, which is exactly how structural formulae stay compact.

options.text: To show the group carries a negative charge
options.explanation: Brackets in structural formulae are a notation for repeats, not a charge symbol.

options.text: Because bracketed groups are unreactive
options.explanation: Reactivity is unrelated to the bracket notation used in structural formulae.

options.text: Because brackets convert it into a displayed formula
options.explanation: A displayed formula needs every bond drawn; brackets are the shortcut that defines a structural formula.

lessons.title: Families, functional groups and isomers
lessons.opening: Chemists sort the thousands of organic compounds into families that behave alike. This lesson defines the three sorting words the exam rewards: homologous series, functional group and isomerism.
keyPoints: A homologous series is a family of compounds with the same functional group and similar chemical properties.
Members of a homologous series share one general formula and differ by a CH2 unit between neighbours.
Physical properties change gradually across a homologous series, a pattern called gradation.
A functional group is the bonded arrangement of atoms that decides how the family reacts.
Isomers share one molecular formula but differ in their displayed formulae, like propene and cyclopropane.

low.restatement: A homologous series is a chemical family whose members share a functional group, a general formula and step-by-step properties. Isomers are different compounds that happen to share one molecular formula.
low.analogy: A homologous series is like a boy-band lineup where each new member adds exactly one fixed costume piece; isomers are two bands wearing identical costumes but arranged differently on stage.
low.examPointer: Name all three shared features when describing a homologous series: same functional group, same general formula, gradation in properties.

medium.restatement: A homologous series is a family of organic compounds with the same functional group, the same general formula and similar chemistry, whose physical properties grade gradually and whose formulae rise by CH2 per member. Isomers carry the same molecular formula but differ in displayed formulae, which can give them different properties.
medium.analogy: Think of a staircase where each step adds one CH2 block and shifts boiling point slightly: same design, gradual change. Isomers are two buildings from the identical brick count assembled on different footprints.
medium.examPointer: For isomer questions, count atoms first and then compare how the bonds are arranged; identical counts with different arrangements is the whole claim.

check.stem: What makes two compounds members of the same homologous series?

options.text: They share the same functional group and so react similarly
options.explanation: The shared functional group is what hands the whole family its similar chemical properties.

options.text: They have identical molecular formulae
options.explanation: Identical molecular formulae would make them isomers or the same compound, not series neighbours.

options.text: They dissolve in the same solvents
options.explanation: Solvent behaviour is not the defining test; the functional group is.

options.text: They were discovered in the same decade
options.explanation: History of discovery plays no part in the definition.

check.stem: How do neighbouring members of a homologous series differ?

options.text: Their molecular formulae differ by one CH2 unit
options.explanation: Each step along the series adds one carbon and two hydrogens.

options.text: Their molecular formulae differ by one CH4 unit
options.explanation: The step is CH2; adding CH4 would skip the count the series actually follows.

options.text: They change functional group at every step
options.explanation: The functional group stays fixed; changing it would leave the series.

options.text: They differ only in physical state at room temperature
options.explanation: State changes do occur gradually, but the formula difference is the defining step.

options.text: A bonded arrangement of atoms that governs the reactions of its family
options.explanation: The specific arrangement of atoms is what steers the characteristic chemistry of the series.

options.text: Any atom at the end of a chain
options.explanation: Position at a chain end is irrelevant; the specific bonded arrangement defines the group.

options.text: The largest atom in the molecule
options.explanation: Atomic size has nothing to do with the functional group concept.

options.text: The bonds that a molecule has broken
options.explanation: Functional groups describe intact bonding arrangements, not broken ones.

check.stem: Propene and cyclopropane both have the molecular formula C3H6. What are they?

options.text: Isomers, because the same formula is arranged in different displayed structures
options.explanation: Same molecular formula with different bonding arrangements is exactly the isomer definition.

options.text: The same compound drawn twice
options.explanation: The ring versus chain arrangements are genuinely different compounds with different properties.

options.text: Members of different homologous series with different formulae
options.explanation: Their formulae are identical; the series differ, but the shared formula is the point.

options.text: Unrelated because one is cyclic
options.explanation: A ring shape does not break the isomer relationship; it is precisely what makes the structures differ.

check.stem: What does gradation mean for a homologous series?

options.text: Physical properties change step by step along the series
options.explanation: Boiling point and viscosity drift smoothly as the chain grows one CH2 at a time.

options.text: Every member has identical physical properties
options.explanation: Chemical properties are similar across the series, but physical ones shift gradually.

options.text: Properties change randomly with no pattern
options.explanation: The pattern is exactly the point: gradual, predictable change along the family.

options.text: Each member reacts faster than the last without exception
options.explanation: Gradation describes the trend in physical properties, not a universal rate speed-up.

glossary.definition: A compound whose molecules contain hydrogen and carbon atoms only, with no other element present.
A formula showing the simplest possible whole-number ratio of the atoms in a molecule.
A drawing that shows every atom and every bond in a molecule, also called the graphical formula.
A family of organic compounds with the same functional group, similar properties and formulae differing by CH2.
The existence of compounds that share one molecular formula but have different displayed formulae.
